# EmbedIQ — Setup Guide

This guide explains how to install and activate the AI coding agent harness EmbedIQ just generated for **Enterprise services platform**. Follow the section that matches each agent your team uses.

## What was generated

- Path-scoped rules and hooks tailored to your stack and compliance posture.
- Permission tiers matched to your security tolerance.
- Local-AI integration files (Ollama, Continue.dev, Aider, Zed AI) for air-gapped operation.
## Install and activate each agent

### Claude Code

Files: `CLAUDE.md` (project memory), `.claude/settings.json` (team settings), `.claude/settings.local.json` (personal overrides, gitignored), `.claude/rules/`, `.claude/commands/`, `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/hooks/`.

- Install Claude Code: `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | sh` (or via Homebrew: `brew install --cask claude-code`).
- Open this repository in your terminal and run `claude` — Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md` automatically.
- Add `.claude/settings.local.json` to your `.gitignore` (it should already be there). It contains your personal permission tier and shouldn't be shared.
- In Claude Code, type `/rules` to see the active rule list. Type `/commands` to see custom slash commands.
- Verify hooks are active: run `claude --help` and confirm "PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks enabled" appears in the startup banner.
### Local AI (Ollama)

Files: `OLLAMA.md` (setup runbook). If `Continue.dev` / `Aider` / `Zed AI` are selected, additional config files were written.

- Install Ollama: `curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh` (Linux/macOS) or download from [ollama.com](https://ollama.com).
- Pull the recommended models per `OLLAMA.md` (the runbook lists exact `ollama pull` commands).
- Start the Ollama daemon: `ollama serve` (runs on `localhost:11434` by default).
- Air-gapped: skip the `pull` step on the air-gapped host; instead, `ollama pull` on a connected machine, then transfer `~/.ollama/models/` to the target host.
## Verification — confirm the harness is wired correctly

- Open the generated `CLAUDE.md` (or `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md` / etc.) and confirm the project name, languages, and frameworks are correct.
- In your agent of choice, ask: "What compliance frameworks am I configured for?" — the answer should include: general best practices
- Try editing a file in a protected directory. The agent should refuse or surface a blocking hook message.
## Common troubleshooting

- **Rules don't seem to apply** — the agent often caches rules at startup. Restart the IDE / CLI session after adding or editing rule files.
- **Permission denied errors on hooks** — Python hooks must be executable. Run `chmod +x .claude/hooks/*.py` from the repo root.
- **Settings.local.json not respected** — Claude Code only reads it when the file is at the repository root in `.claude/`. Confirm path and re-check `.gitignore` excludes it from commits.
- **Configuration drifted** — run `make drift` from the EmbedIQ repository to compare the current state against the expected harness. The drift report flags what changed.
- **Need to regenerate** — re-run the EmbedIQ wizard with the same answers. Output is deterministic — re-running with the same inputs always produces byte-identical files.
## Keeping the harness in sync with policy changes

When your team's policies change (new compliance framework, new domain pack, updated permission tier), re-run the EmbedIQ wizard with the updated answers. The new harness is byte-identical for unchanged answers and differs only where your input changed.

- Re-run interactively: `npm start` from the EmbedIQ repository (or `make start`).
- Re-run headlessly via the web API: `POST /api/generate` with the updated answer set.
- Continuous monitoring: set up the EmbedIQ autopilot to scan this repository on a schedule and open a PR when drift is detected.
